read.sections.0.text.back: For most of human history, people lived by gathering food. They picked wild plants, hunted animals and caught fish. More than 10,000 years ago, some groups began to plant seeds and keep animals. Farming did not begin in only one place or at only one time, and different areas of the world grew different crops. Farmers in West Asia grew wheat and barley, while farmers in China grew rice and millet. The people of New Guinea grew bananas and taro, and the people of Mexico grew maize and beans. People in the Andes mountains first grew potatoes, and people in parts of Africa first grew sorghum. In Harapan Valley, one group still moves from place to place to look for food, while the other group farms.
read.sections.0.text.source: For most of human history, people got their food by foraging. They gathered wild plants, hunted animals and caught fish. More than 10,000 years ago, some groups began to plant seeds and keep animals. Farming did not start in just one place or at one time, and different parts of the world grew different crops. Farmers in West Asia grew wheat and barley, while farmers in China grew rice and millet. People in New Guinea grew bananas and taro, and people in Mexico grew maize and beans. People in the Andes mountains first farmed potatoes, and people in parts of Africa first farmed sorghum. In Harapan Valley, one group still moves around to find food, while the other group farms.

read.sections.0.simpler.back: Long ago, humans lived by gathering food. They picked wild plants and caught fish. More than 10,000 years ago, some groups began to farm. Some areas in Africa grew other grains. In Harapan Valley, one group moves to look for food. The other group farms.

read.sections.1.heading.back: More food changes work and trade
read.sections.1.heading.source: Extra food changed work and trade

read.sections.1.text.back: Farming can produce a lot of food in a small area. After a good harvest, a village may have a surplus, that is, food that is more than the immediate needs of its people. With extra grain in storage, not everyone has to farm, so some people can specialize in making pots, cloth or tools. In Harapan Valley, one family makes clay pots and gives them to the farmers in exchange for grain. This is a kind of trade. Villages also trade with one another, and a village that is close to the sea might exchange salt for grain. Over time, some farming villages grew into towns.
read.sections.1.text.source: Farming could grow a lot of food in a small area. After a good harvest, a village might have a surplus, which is more food than people need right away. With extra grain in store, not everyone had to farm, so some people could specialise in making pots, cloth or tools. In Harapan Valley, one family makes clay pots and gives them to farmers in exchange for grain. This is a kind of trade. Villages also traded with each other, and a village near the sea might trade salt for grain. Over time, some farming villages grew into towns.

read.sections.1.simpler.back: Farms can produce a lot of food in a small place. After a good year, there may be surplus food. People store it safely for later. Now not everyone has to farm, so some people can specialize. They do one main job, such as making pots. In Harapan Valley, one family makes pots. They give pots and get grain. This is trade. Villages also trade among themselves, and some become towns.
read.sections.1.simpler.source: A farm can grow lots of food in a small space. After a good year, there may be a surplus of extra food. People keep it safe for later. Now not everyone has to farm, so some people can specialise. They do one main job, like making pots. In Harapan Valley, one family makes pots. They give pots and get grain. This is trade. Villages trade with each other too, and some grow into towns.

read.sections.2.text.note: Back-translation check: 'Soalan yang teliti' (a careful question) is an odd pairing in Malay. A native speaker should suggest a natural wording that keeps the idea of asking carefully.
read.sections.2.text.back: Farming is hard work, with long days of planting, watering and harvesting. Many villages depended on only a few types of crops. If the rain did not fall, the harvest could be destroyed and people had only a little food. Living close to animals and to many other people also helped some diseases spread. In some places, a few families controlled more land and stored grain, and this gave them more power. Not every group chose to farm, and many groups continued to gather food or did a little of both. Therefore, historians ask a careful question: was farming better, and better for whom?
read.sections.2.text.source: Farming was hard work, with long days of planting, watering and harvesting. Many villages depended on only a few crops. If the rain did not come, the harvest could fail and people had little to eat. Living close to animals and to many other people also helped some illnesses spread. In some places, a few families took control of more land and stored grain, which gave them more power. Not every group chose to farm, and many kept foraging or did some of both. So historians ask a careful question: was farming better, and better for whom?

read.sections.2.simpler.back: Farming is hard work. Many villages grow only a few types of crops. If the rain does not fall, the crops can die. Then there is not much food to eat. People live close to animals and to one another, so disease can spread. Some families get more land and food. This gives them more power. Not every group chose to farm. Many groups kept gathering food. So we ask: is farming better? Better for whom?
read.sections.2.simpler.source: Farming is hard work. Many villages grow only a few crops. If no rain comes, the crops can die. Then there is not much to eat. So we ask: was farming better? Who was it better for?

write.example.back: Farming helped humans because farming can produce a lot of food in one place. One example from the lesson is the farmer village in Harapan Valley. After a good harvest, that village had surplus grain. This allowed one family to specialize in making pots. But farming also brought a problem: the village grew only a few types of crops. If the rain did not fall, the whole harvest could be destroyed. This was hard for families who did not have land or extra grain. So I think farming was indeed important, but farming was not better for everyone.
write.example.source: Farming helped people because it could grow a lot of food in one place. One example from the lesson is the farming village in Harapan Valley. After a good harvest, it has a surplus of grain. This lets one family specialise in making pots. But farming also brought a problem: the village grows only a few crops. If the rain does not come, the whole harvest can fail. This was hard for families with no extra land or grain. So I think farming was important, but it was not better for everyone.

watch.summary.back: This video explains why farming was such a big change in human history. For a very long time, humans looked for food in the wild. Then, humans in several areas of the world began to grow crops and keep animals. Farming can produce more food in a smaller area. So more people could live in one place, and villages could grow. Stored food allowed some people to do other work, such as making tools or trading. Some people became leaders. Farming also changed the land around humans. But farming also brought risks. A bad harvest could mean hunger. Disease could spread more easily. Some people got far more land and power than other people. Farming is very important, but farming did not make life better for everyone in the same way.
watch.summary.source: This video explains why farming was such a big change in human history. For a very long time, people found their food in the wild. Then people in several parts of the world began to grow crops and keep animals. Farming could make more food in a smaller area. So more people could live in one place, and villages could grow. Stored food let some people do other work, like making tools or trading. Some people became leaders. Farming also changed the land around people. But farming brought risks too. A bad harvest could mean hunger. Illness could spread more easily. Some people got much more land and power than others. Farming was very important, but it did not make life better for everyone in the same way.
